alignments.note: Conjunction waw → And (rule 14).
Article → the (rule 15).
Noun.
Relative אֲשֶׁר → that.

בְּתוֹךְ is rendered by the single English preposition among, so the preposition and the construct noun fuse (rule 30); the supplied copula is of the verbless clause and joins this prepositional predicate (rules 20, 49), which rule 30 allows the fused unit to carry, as in לִפְנֵי → was before. Head on the lexeme-bearing תָּוֶךְ / among.
Pronominal suffix → them (rule 18).
Finite verb with its auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24). Discontinuous with the following prepositional phrase in English order.
אֶל rendered upon (rule 11).

No pronominal suffix or other possessive morpheme stands on כָּתֵף, which is anarthrous, so the supplied possessive his answers to no source morpheme and is added (rules 18, 30). The competing reading folds his into the noun's unit as part of an English possessive phrase; I did not take it, because rule 18 reserves that only for a present suffix, and contrast the his at t043, which the ASV writes where a real article morpheme stands (rule 41).
Noun → shoulder.
Preposition בְּ → in (rule 11).
Assimilated article token → the written the (rules 12, 15).
עֲלָטָה → dark.
Waw of the consecutive form → and (rule 14).
Verb with auxiliary and phrasal particle forth, which is not a complement, so the head stays on the lexical verb go (rule 44).

3mp verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24). English fronts the clause's verb before the prepositional phrase, so this unit precedes s016–s018 in target order (rule 25).
בְּ rendered through with the verb of digging (rule 11).
Assimilated article token → the (rule 12).
קִיר → wall.
Purpose לְ before the infinitive construct, rendered by the English infinitive marker to (rules 11, 52).
Hiphil infinitive construct with its phrasal particle out; head on the lexical verb (rule 44).

בוֹ fused into the single English word thereby, so preposition and suffix share one unit (rule 30). Source head on the preposition as the syntactic head of the pair; heading it on the suffix, which carries the referential there-, is defensible, but the preposition governs the phrase.
Verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
פָּנֶה → face.
Pronominal suffix → his (rule 18).

The fixed compound conjunction יַעַן אֲשֶׁר is rendered by the one English word because, so both morphemes share one unit headed on the lexeme-bearing יַעַן (rule 30). The competing reading gives because to יַעַן and marks אֲשֶׁר unrepresented under rule 22; I did not take it, because rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and no morpheme owns a part of because.
Negative לֹא → not.
Verb with its auxiliary, discontinuous around the negative (rule 25); the subject pronoun he belongs to the explicit הוּא. Head on the lexical verb.
Explicit subject pronoun הוּא → he; the written pronoun takes the English subject pronoun and the verb keeps only its auxiliary and lexeme (rule 20's explicit-subject clause).
Definite direct-object marker: the ASV writes the object bare (see the land), so no English word answers to the object relation (rule 16).
Article → the (rule 15).
אֶרֶץ → land.
Instrumental לְ rendered with (rule 11).

The assimilated article on לַעַיִן: the ASV writes no the for the phrase but a possessive his standing where the phrase's the would stand, so the article takes it (rules 12, 41). No suffix stands on עַיִן to license that possessive instead.
עַיִן → eyes; the English plural does not affect the alignment.

review_notes: Two supplied possessives are treated differently on purpose: t011 his has no article and no suffix behind it and is added under rule 18, while t043 his stands where a real assimilated article morpheme is present and is that article's rendering under rule 41.

בְּתוֹךְ (s005–s006) is fused under rule 30 and carries the verbless clause's copula; יַעַן אֲשֶׁר (s027–s028) is fused on the same one-English-word condition, with the rule 22 alternative named in its note.
English clause order puts the verb יַחְתְּרוּ before its prepositional phrase, so s016–s018 follow s019 in target position; the units themselves are contiguous.
